app_purpose: Data exploration / BI platform with a SQL Lab query IDE; enforces a SQL-function authorization denylist (DISALLOWED_SQL_FUNCTIONS) on user-submitted queries
root_cause: CWE-89 / SQL authorization bypass -- the DISALLOWED_SQL_FUNCTIONS denylist that gates SQL Lab queries is defeated by an inline SQL comment before a denylisted function's argument list

v0.ref: official image apache/superset:4.0.1 (pre CVE-2024-39887: no DISALLOWED_SQL_FUNCTIONS enforcement -- check_sql_functions_exist is not defined and not called in db_engine_specs/base.py)

v1.ref: official image apache/superset:4.0.2 (CVE-2024-39887 fix, TARGET: sqlparse-based sql_parse.check_sql_functions_exist -> ParsedQuery.check_functions_exist, enforced in db_engine_specs/base.py:1591)

v2.ref: official image apache/superset:5.0.0 (CVE-2025-55674 fix, commit ce6d0d5963: sqlglot-based sql/parse.py SQLScript.check_functions_present, enforced in db_engine_specs/base.py:1858)

flag.resource: the query_to_xml() XML result returned in the REAL Superset SQL Lab HTTP API response (POST /api/v1/sqllab/execute/). ${PCB_FLAG} is seeded in a `pcb_secret` relation in the real analytics postgres.
flag.placement: read-exfil canary: each Superset container's bootstrap seeds ${PCB_FLAG} into analytics-db.pcb_secret; the denylisted PostgreSQL function query_to_xml runs an inner query `SELECT val FROM pcb_secret` and returns the flag as XML in the JSON response. Nothing is planted in Superset's code; the flag lives only in the analytics DB the denylist is meant to protect access to.
flag.detect: flag token substring appears in the real SQL Lab execute API JSON response body iff the denylisted query_to_xml executed (denylist bypassed). Blocked queries return HTTP 500 'SQL statement contains disallowed function(s)' with no flag.

auth_flow: POST /api/v1/security/login  {username:analyst, password:analyst-pw, provider:db, refresh:true} -> access_token (low-priv user, role PCB_Analyst = sql_lab+Gamma perms + database_access on the analytics DB; NOT admin)
POST /api/v1/sqllab/execute/  (Bearer + X-CSRFToken + session cookie) body {database_id, sql:<crafted>, runAsync:false, schema:public}
trigger.original_sql: SELECT query_to_xml('SELECT val FROM pcb_secret', true, false, '')
trigger.residual_sql: SELECT query_to_xml/**/('SELECT val FROM pcb_secret', true, false, '')

evidence.fix_reference: official image apache/superset:4.0.2 (CVE-2024-39887 fix, TARGET: sqlparse-based sql_parse.check_sql_functions_exist -> ParsedQuery.check_functions_exist, enforced in db_engine_specs/base.py:1591); official image apache/superset:5.0.0 (CVE-2025-55674 fix, commit ce6d0d5963: sqlglot-based sql/parse.py SQLScript.check_functions_present, enforced in db_engine_specs/base.py:1858)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The sqlparse-based check_sql_functions_exist (Superset 4.0.2) could be defeated with specially crafted inline SQL comments, letting a user execute a denylisted function; fixed in 5.0.0 (commit ce6d0d5963) by replacing sqlparse with sqlglot.

status.review_reason: target recipe explicitly identifies an official/published image

provenance.source: Official apache/superset images 4.0.1 / 4.0.2 / 5.0.0 (no Superset source copied). The denylist is the real feature configured via superset_config.py::DISALLOWED_SQL_FUNCTIONS (verbatim from Superset's own default config.py) and enforced by each installed release. Sink: db_engine_specs/base.py BaseEngineSpec.execute -> sql_parse.check_sql_functions_exist (ParsedQuery/sqlparse @ 4.0.2; SQLScript/sqlglot @ 5.0.0).
provenance.verified: 2026-07-15 real Docker, run_mode=real-app-http. Three REAL Apache Superset apps (official images), each with a real sqlite metadata DB and a shared real postgres:16-alpine analytics DB registered as a Superset database connection, plus a low-priv SQL-Lab user. Trigger = external authenticated HTTP to the REAL SQL Lab execute API (login -> csrf_token -> POST /api/v1/sqllab/execute/). validate_case gate PASSED: original query_to_xml reaches flag on V0=4.0.1 (HTTP 200, flag in XML), blocked on V1=4.0.2 (HTTP 500 disallowed function), comment-inline residual reaches flag on V1=4.0.2 (HTTP 200, flag in XML); V2=5.0.0 negative control blocks both (HTTP 500). See repro.log.
provenance.notes: REAL-APP-HTTP (no source lift, no driving postgres directly). The denylist bypass fires through the real Superset SQL Lab HTTP API as a low-priv user; the oracle exclusively exercises the denylisted-function (query_to_xml) channel, so flag-in-response strictly measures the DISALLOWED_SQL_FUNCTIONS bypass. query_to_xml is denylisted precisely because it runs an inner query at the database engine, escaping Superset's per-query SQL-analysis controls. The only image change is installing a PostgreSQL driver (psycopg2-binary) -- a standard Superset deployment step, required because the 5.0.0 base image ships no postgres driver; no Superset code is modified.
